design_detail: Short report of a laboratory selectivity and sensitivity study of four brands of urine fentanyl immunoassay strips (BTNX Rapid Response, cut-off 20 ng/mL; Rapid Self Test FYL20, 20 ng/mL; Nal van Minden Drug-Screen FYL 10, 10 ng/mL; Hangzhou Alltest One Step FYL20 dipstick, 20 ng/mL) on single-compound solutions of reference compounds in Type 1 water, at one laboratory in Oslo. Fentanyl was tested at 10–1000 ng/mL; 28 fentanyl analogues at 100 and 1000 ng/mL, and at 10,000 ng/mL (carfentanil 4000 ng/mL) for compounds not clearly positive at 1000; three non-fentanyl synthetic opioids (U-47700, U-48800, U-50488), methadone and eight other drugs (amphetamine, cocaine, heroin, LSD, MDMA, methamphetamine, morphine, THC) at 100 and 1000 ng/mL. Fentanyl, carfentanil and remifentanil (1000 ng/mL) were also tested with heroin (50,000 ng/mL) or ascorbic acid (75 mg/mL), ascorbic acid alone at 0–75 mg/mL, and four analogues at 10 ng/mL alone and mixed (one brand). Strips were dipped for 13–20 s as the urine instructions state and graded by the authors on a four-level scale. Filed as test-accuracy (METHODS §5.3, version 0.3.1): the units are prepared solutions, and the study is appraised with QUADAS-2 because strip readings are compared with known content, as in sc_green_2020; the reference is the known preparation, not a second analytical method. The online supplement (compound list and sources, procedural detail, supplementary figures) was not read.
can_establish: Which of 28 fentanyl analogues and 12 other drugs four brands of urine fentanyl strips reacted to, as pure single compounds in water at set concentrations read by the authors, how strongly detection depended on concentration and on the reading rule, and whether heroin, ascorbic acid or a mixture of low-level analogues changed the reading.
cannot_establish: How accurate the strips are on street drug samples prepared and read by people who check drugs, how often undetected analogues occur in any drug market, lot-to-lot or reader variation (no replicates reported), cross-reactivity with non-fentanyl drugs above 1000 ng/mL or with cutting agents other than ascorbic acid, or any effect on behaviour or overdose.

sample.recruitment: Not people or street samples: compounds bought from commercial distributors (see Table 1 and the supplement, not read) and dissolved in Type 1 water (Methods › Chemicals; Preparation of drug solutions, p. 2). n_total counts the 41 compounds tested (editors' count).
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Analogues described as currently on the recreational drug market, among them the pharmaceutical fentanyls alfentanil, remifentanil and sufentanil, carfentanil, and the related compounds norcarfentanil and despropionyl-2-fluorofentanyl; the rule for choosing the panel is not stated.
sample.demographics: Not applicable (solutions).
sample.attrition: Not every compound was tested at every concentration: five analogues (alfentanil, despropionyl-2-fluorofentanyl, norcarfentanil, remifentanil, sufentanil) were not measured at 100 ng/mL but are counted as negative in that column's totals, and 10,000 ng/mL was tested only for compounds not clearly positive at 1000 ng/mL (editors' reading of Table 1, p. 2). Strip lots, replicates and the number of strips per condition are not reported in the main text.
sample.selection_effects: Pure single compounds in water at fixed concentrations are the conditions most favourable to clear readings and the least like street samples, which hold unknown amounts with mixtures and cutting agents. The analogue panel is not weighted by how often each compound occurs in any market, so the number of analogues detected says nothing about the share of real samples a strip would flag.

exposure.measurement: Index tests: four urine fentanyl strip brands, bought for the study, dipped for 13–20 s per the makers' urine instructions (Methods › Fentanyl test strips; Fentanyl test strip experiments, p. 2). Reading: the makers' instructions call a test negative whenever a test band appears, whatever its intensity (Results › Interpretation of test results; Fig. 1A, p. 3). After seeing concentration-dependent bands, the authors graded ‘++’ clearly positive (no test band), ‘+’ positive (barely visible test band), ‘(+)’ weak positive or ambiguous (faint test band) and ‘−’ negative (solid test band), and counted ++ and + as positive (p. 3).
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Not applicable (no dosing). Test concentrations: fentanyl 10–1000 ng/mL; analogues 100, 1000 and 10,000 ng/mL, carfentanil 4000 ng/mL, chosen from a cited estimate (Casale et al., 2017) that 20 μg of carfentanil, about 4000 ng/mL in 5 mL, is potentially life-threatening; other drugs 100 and 1000 ng/mL; heroin 50,000 ng/mL; ascorbic acid 0–75 mg/mL, included because acids are used when heroin base is prepared for injection (cited study); four-analogue mixture at 10 ng/mL each (Preparation of drug solutions, p. 2).
exposure.polysubstance: Single compounds, except fentanyl, carfentanil and remifentanil each with heroin or with ascorbic acid, and a mixture of acetyl-, acryl-, furanyl- and butyrfentanyl at 10 ng/mL each tested with Nal van Minden only. No cutting agents other than ascorbic acid and no stimulant–fentanyl mixtures.

comparison.controls: Reference: the known content of each prepared solution; Type 1 water as negative control and fentanyl 1000 ng/mL as positive control (Fig. 1B, p. 3). No analytical check of the prepared concentrations is reported in the main text.
comparison.matching: Not applicable; all four brands were tested on the same solutions.
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Not applicable to solutions. Not reported in the main text: strip lots and expiry dates, number of replicates, who read the strips and whether readers knew the content, reading time, and agreement between readers.

outcomes.instruments: Visual grading of each strip on the authors' four-level scale; for each brand and concentration, the number of the 28 analogues graded positive (++ or +), weak or ambiguous, and negative (Table 1, p. 2); results for the other drugs and for the heroin, ascorbic acid and mixture experiments in the text and Figs. 1–2.
outcomes.validity_norms: The makers' cut-offs (10 or 20 ng/mL) refer to urine; use on drug solutions is off-label. The authors' grading departs from the makers' reading rule, and no reliability between readers or runs is reported.
outcomes.operationalization: Positive = no test band or a barely visible one (++ or +); faint band = weak positive or ambiguous; solid band = negative. The 10,000 ng/mL totals are cumulative over 1000 and 10,000 ng/mL (Table 1 note a).
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: Not applicable (descriptive; no statistics).
outcomes.assessor_blinding: Not reported; nothing in the main text suggests that readers were blind to the solutions.

analysis.effect_sizes: No statistics; counts only (Table 1, p. 2). By the authors' counting rule (++ or + positive), analogues detected at 100 ng/mL: Rapid Response 5, Rapid Self Test 5, One Step 12, Nal van Minden 9 (of the 23 actually measured, editors' count; the printed totals count the 5 unmeasured as negative); at 1000 ng/mL 21, 19, 15 and 22 of 28; cumulative to 10,000 ng/mL 24, 24, 21 and 24 of 28. Editors' recount by the makers' rule as the paper describes it (only ++, no test band, positive): at 100 ng/mL 1, 2, 11 and 4 of 23; at 1000 ng/mL 18, 16, 14 and 20 of 28; cumulative 20, 20, 19 and 21 of 28; fentanyl itself at 100 ng/mL was + (a barely visible band) on Rapid Response and Rapid Self Test. Editors' recount reading faint bands as presence, as the authors recommend: 13, 9, 14 and 15 of 23 at 100 ng/mL; cumulative 25, 25, 21 and 25 of 28. Editors' calculation (Wilson 95% CI, treating the panel as if it were sampled, which it is not): 24/28 = 85.7% (68.5–94.3%); 21/28 = 75.0% (56.6–87.3%). No positive results from the 12 non-fentanyl drugs at 100 and 1000 ng/mL on any brand; One Step positive with ascorbic acid alone at 10, 25 and 75 mg/mL, not at 1.5 mg/mL. Fentanyl itself, in the descending series pictured for two brands (Fig. 1C, p. 3): lowest positive reading 50 ng/mL (Rapid Response) and 25 ng/mL (One Step) by the authors' rule, 100 and 50 ng/mL by the makers' rule.
analysis.preregistration_detail: No protocol or registration is mentioned.
analysis.selective_reporting: The additive-mixture result is reported for one brand only and generalized to all brands by expectation; heroin and ascorbic acid were tested with three compounds at one concentration; results for the non-fentanyl drugs are given in one sentence without a table; procedural detail and supplementary figures are in the online supplement (not read).
analysis.power: Not applicable. No replicates are reported, so the reproducibility of single cells, especially borderline + and (+) readings, is unknown.

interpretation_gap.results_show: All four brands reacted to fentanyl, and to most of the 28 analogues at 1000 ng/mL or more (21–24 of 28 by the authors' counting rule), but to far fewer at 100 ng/mL (5–12 of the 23 measured, editors' count). No brand reacted to alfentanil, despropionyl-2-fluorofentanyl or norcarfentanil; carfentanil read positive on no brand at 1000 ng/mL (a faint test band, weak or ambiguous, on three brands; a solid band, negative, on One Step) and was clearly positive at 4000 ng/mL on three brands, never on One Step. Detection depended on concentration and on how faint bands are read: by the makers' rule the counts are lower. No reactions to 12 non-fentanyl drugs at up to 1000 ng/mL; ascorbic acid at 10 mg/mL or more gave false positives on One Step; heroin changed nothing.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The abstract states that “All test strips detected fentanyl as well as 21–24 of the 28 fentanyl analogues” (p. 1) without saying that these counts use 1000–10,000 ng/mL and the authors' own reading of barely visible bands as positive; at 100 ng/mL detection was 5–12 of the 23 measured (editors' count). The Conclusion's “detecting the vast majority of the fentanyl analogues present on the recreational drug market” (p. 4) generalizes from a panel not weighted by market occurrence. The recommendation to read faint bands as presence was not tested for its effect on false positives, and the recommendation to test injection solutions without further dilution (p. 4) is not reconciled with the authors' own finding that ascorbic acid, which they included to model injection solutions, gave false positives on One Step. The abstract's caution that the strips are no panacea, because some analogues are missed, is supported.

timeline.event: Casale et al. (2017): analysis of illicit carfentanil, cited for the estimate that 20 μg can be life-threatening, which set the 4000 ng/mL test concentration; not read.
McGowan et al. (2018), cited as background on whether enough is known to promote fentanyl self-testing outside supervised settings; not read.

Green et al. (2020): BTNX strips detected fentanyl in 104 of 106 police-seized samples and were positive in all four exploratory samples containing acetyl fentanyl or furanyl fentanyl (card sc_green_2020), consistent with detection of these analogues here at 1000 ng/mL; that study also recorded strip positives in seized samples negative for fentanyl by GC/MS.
This study (volume 90; copyright 2020).

Lockwood et al. (2021): solutions of seized methamphetamine and MDMA and of retail diphenhydramine gave false positives on BTNX Rapid Response strips at about 1–2.5 mg/mL of material, 1000 to 2500 times the 1000 ng/mL ceiling tested here. Read in this round (card sc_lockwood_2021).

Sisco et al. (2024b) cite this study among laboratory studies of strip false positives and analogue detection; read in this round (card sc_sisco_2024b), though it did not test fentanyl-strip cross-reactivity.

Halifax et al. (2024): five lots of BTNX Rapid Response strips detected 11 of 13 fentanyl analogues, never alfentanil, and carfentanil on every lot but on two lots obtained in 2021 only from 10 000 ng/mL; pure d-methamphetamine and MDMA gave false positives at mg/mL concentrations. Read in this round (card sc_halifax_2024).

replication.where_it_stands: Detection of acetyl and furanyl fentanyl is consistent with the seized-sample study (Green et al., 2020). Five lots of the BTNX strip in another laboratory also detected most of a 13-analogue panel, never alfentanil, and carfentanil on every lot but on two newer lots only from 10 000 ng/mL (Halifax et al., 2024), which agrees with the carfentanil gap here. Methamphetamine and MDMA, negative here at up to 1000 ng/mL, gave false positives at mg/mL concentrations in two other laboratories (Lockwood et al., 2021; Halifax et al., 2024), so the studies do not conflict, but this study cannot exclude cross-reactivity at higher concentrations. The One Step ascorbic acid artefact has no independent check among the papers read.

funding.funder: No funding statement beyond the Acknowledgments: M.H. Baumann is funded by the Intramural Research Program of the National Institute on Drug Abuse, National Institutes of Health (p. 5). The strips were purchased for the study (p. 2).
funding.declared_conflicts: The authors declare no conflicts of interest related to the study (Declarations of Interests, p. 5).
funding.affiliations_note: Authors from the Section for Drug Abuse Research, Department of Forensic Sciences, Oslo University Hospital, the University of Oslo (Department of Chemistry; Institute of Basic Medical Sciences) and the Designer Drug Research Unit of the NIDA Intramural Research Program, Baltimore. No link to a strip maker is declared. Open access under a CC BY licence. A flag for closer reading, not a reason to discount.

what_would_settle_it: Replicate testing of several lots of each brand, read blind by trained and untrained readers under both the makers' and the authors' reading rules, on street samples and on solutions prepared as they are in drug-checking practice (with mixtures, cutting agents, acids and stimulants at realistic concentrations), against quantitative LC-MS/MS, with analogues weighted by how often they appear in current drug-checking data.

preclinical.species_strain_sex: Not applicable (prepared drug solutions; no animals or cells).
preclinical.dose_route_schedule: Not applicable (no dosing); test concentrations as in the exposure fields.
preclinical.resembles_human_use: Partly: the strips and the makers' urine instructions are those used in drug checking, but the samples were pure single compounds of known concentration in laboratory water, read by laboratory scientists, whereas street samples contain unknown amounts with mixtures and cutting agents; the authors note that the dilution described in community guidance would give lower concentrations than an injection solution (Discussion, 3rd paragraph, p. 4).

domains.note: Prepared single-compound solutions of reference materials at fixed concentrations, not street samples; a chosen analogue panel; negatives limited to 12 drugs at up to 1000 ng/mL plus ascorbic acid. Known-positive and known-negative solutions are a case-control-like design that favours clear results; applicability to drug checking is low.

Readers are not described and probably knew the content; the four-level grading was devised after seeing concentration-dependent results, and its threshold (++ or +) differs from the makers' rule; lots, replicates and reading time are not reported in the main text; Table 1 and Fig. 1C grade the same result (Rapid Response, fentanyl 100 ng/mL) differently (+ v ++).
Content known by preparation from commercial reference compounds; the concentrations are not reported as verified, a minor concern.

Not every compound was tested at every concentration: five analogues not measured at 100 ng/mL are counted as negative; 10,000 ng/mL only for compounds not clearly positive at 1000; carfentanil's 4000 ng/mL result sits in the 10,000 column; the co-presence experiments used three compounds and the mixture experiment one brand.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: QUADAS-2 is used because strip readings are compared with known content (METHODS §5.3, diagnostic accuracy); the design is filed as test-accuracy (METHODS §5.3, version 0.3.1). The overall judgment follows the worst domains (artificial samples; unblinded, post hoc grading with a non-standard threshold). These problems mostly favour detection, so the study is better evidence of what the strips miss (three analogues entirely, carfentanil below 4000 ng/mL on the authors' counting rule, most analogues at 100 ng/mL) than of how often they would flag analogues in real samples. Citable for: each brand's reactions to each of the 28 analogues at the concentrations tested, under a stated reading rule; no reaction to alfentanil, despropionyl-2-fluorofentanyl or norcarfentanil; strong dependence on concentration and on the reading rule; no reaction to 12 non-fentanyl drugs at up to 1000 ng/mL; false positives with ascorbic acid on One Step; no effect of heroin. Not citable for: accuracy on street samples or when people test, the share of real samples with undetected analogues, other lots or brands, or effects on behaviour or overdose.

key_findings.finding: Four urine fentanyl strip brands were bought and tested: BTNX Rapid Response (cut-off 20 ng/mL), Rapid Self Test FYL20 (20 ng/mL), Nal van Minden Drug-Screen FYL 10 (10 ng/mL) and Hangzhou Alltest One Step FYL20 (20 ng/mL), dipped for 13–20 s in single-compound solutions in Type 1 water: 28 analogues at 100 and 1000 ng/mL and, where needed, 10,000 ng/mL (carfentanil 4000 ng/mL); non-fentanyl drugs at 100 and 1000 ng/mL.
key_findings.locator: Introduction, 3rd paragraph; Methods › Fentanyl test strips; Preparation of drug solutions for fentanyl test strip experiments; Fentanyl test strip experiments

key_findings.finding: The makers' instructions call a strip negative whenever two bands appear, however faint the test band (Fig. 1A). Fentanyl at 1000 ng/mL and water gave clear positive and negative results on all brands, but fentanyl at 10–250 ng/mL gave concentration-dependent bands (Fig. 1C labels: Rapid Response ++ at 250 and 100, + at 50, (+) at 25, − at 10; One Step ++ at 250 to 50, + at 25, (+) at 10). The authors therefore graded ++, +, (+) and − and counted ++ and + as positive.
key_findings.locator: Results › Interpretation of test results, 1st paragraph; Fig. 1
key_findings.note: Table 1 grades Rapid Response with fentanyl at 100 ng/mL as +, Fig. 1C as ++.

key_findings.finding: All brands were positive for fentanyl at 100 and 1000 ng/mL: + on Rapid Response and Rapid Self Test at 100 ng/mL, ++ on One Step and Nal van Minden; ++ on all at 1000 ng/mL.
key_findings.locator: Table 1 (Fentanyl row); Results › Selectivity of fentanyl test strips, 1st paragraph
key_findings.note: A + is a barely visible test band, which the makers' rule as described would read as negative (editors' note).

key_findings.finding: Cumulative over 1000 and 10,000 ng/mL, Rapid Response, Rapid Self Test and Nal van Minden were positive for 24 of 28 analogues, all except alfentanil, despropionyl-2-fluorofentanyl, norcarfentanil and remifentanil (the last weak or ambiguous at 10,000 ng/mL); One Step for 21, missing also benzodioxolefentanyl, carfentanil and sufentanil.
key_findings.locator: Table 1 (summary rows); Results › Selectivity of fentanyl test strips, 1st paragraph

key_findings.finding: At 1000 ng/mL, analogues positive: Rapid Response 21, Rapid Self Test 19, One Step 15 and Nal van Minden 22 of 28 (weak or ambiguous 2, 4, 2 and 1).
key_findings.locator: Table 1 (summary rows); Discussion, 2nd paragraph

key_findings.finding: At 100 ng/mL (5–10 times the cut-offs), analogues positive: One Step 12, Nal van Minden 9, Rapid Response 5 and Rapid Self Test 5 (weak or ambiguous 2, 6, 8 and 4). Only 4-fluoroisobutyrfentanyl, acetylfentanyl, acrylfentanyl and methoxyacetylfentanyl were positive at 100 ng/mL on all four brands (editors' reading of Table 1).
key_findings.locator: Table 1 (summary rows); Results › Sensitivity of fentanyl test strips, 1st paragraph
key_findings.note: Only 23 analogues were measured at 100 ng/mL; the printed negative counts (Rapid Response 15, Rapid Self Test 19, One Step 14, Nal van Minden 13) include the five not measured (editors' count).

key_findings.finding: No brand was positive (++ or +) for carfentanil at 1000 ng/mL: Rapid Response, Rapid Self Test and Nal van Minden gave a weak or ambiguous band and One Step was negative. The first three were clearly positive at 4000 ng/mL, the concentration the authors equate with a potentially life-threatening 20 μg in 5 mL; One Step was negative at every concentration.
key_findings.locator: Table 1 (Carfentanil row and note b); Results › Sensitivity of fentanyl test strips, 2nd paragraph
key_findings.note: Under the authors' own recommendation to read faint bands as presence, the three weak bands at 1000 ng/mL would count as detections (editors' note).

key_findings.finding: Analogues positive only at the highest concentration (editors' reading of Table 1): 4-methoxybutyrfentanyl, carfentanil and sufentanil on Rapid Response; these plus 4-fluorocyclopropylbenzylfentanyl and furanylbenzylfentanyl on Rapid Self Test; carfentanil and sufentanil on Nal van Minden; 2-fluorofentanyl, 3-methylcrotonylfentanyl, 4-methoxybutyrfentanyl, cis-3-methylfentanyl, ocfentanil and valerylfentanyl on One Step.
key_findings.locator: Table 1

key_findings.finding: All brands were negative for U-47700, U-48800, U-50488, methadone, amphetamine, cocaine, heroin, LSD, MDMA, methamphetamine, morphine and THC, each tested at 100 and 1000 ng/mL.
key_findings.locator: Methods › Preparation of drug solutions for fentanyl test strip experiments; Results › Selectivity of fentanyl test strips, 2nd paragraph

key_findings.finding: With ascorbic acid, strips at 25 mg/mL or more looked smeared and pale pink but read as before, except that One Step turned clearly positive for carfentanil and remifentanil; ascorbic acid alone (tested at 0, 1.5, 10, 25 and 75 mg/mL) gave false positives on One Step at 10 mg/mL and above, not at 1.5 mg/mL, and none on the other brands. Heroin (50,000 ng/mL) changed no result.
key_findings.locator: Methods › Preparation of drug solutions for fentanyl test strip experiments (p. 2); Results › The effect of ascorbic acid and heroin on test results, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Fig. 2 (p. 4)
key_findings.note: Fig. 2 shows Rapid Response and One Step only; the legend states that the other two brands were unaffected.

key_findings.finding: Acetyl-, acryl-, furanyl- and butyrfentanyl at 10 ng/mL were each negative or weak alone but positive as a mixture (each 10 ng/mL); tested with Nal van Minden only, and expected by the authors to hold for all brands.
key_findings.locator: Results › Additive effect of fentanyl analogues for test strip results, 1st paragraph

key_findings.finding: The authors depart from the makers' rule, arguing that a faint test band should be read as indicating fentanyls because results were so concentration dependent, and recommend against further dilution of injection solutions before testing, since the dilution described by web stores and harm-reduction organizations would lower concentrations and the chance of detecting carfentanil.
key_findings.locator: Discussion, 2nd and 3rd paragraphs; Conclusion

key_findings.finding: The authors conclude that the strips detect the vast majority of analogues on the market but are highly concentration dependent, are unaffected by heroin, give false positives with ascorbic acid on one brand and detect carfentanil poorly; useful for harm reduction with information on their limits, but no panacea.
key_findings.locator: Abstract › Conclusions; Conclusion

reporting_issues.issue: Table 1's totals at 100 ng/mL count as negative five analogues that were not measured at that concentration (alfentanil, despropionyl-2-fluorofentanyl, norcarfentanil, remifentanil, sufentanil), and the text says all strips were tested with analogue solutions at 100 ng/mL.
reporting_issues.consequence: Denominators at 100 ng/mL are 23 measured analogues, not 28; treating compounds negative at 1000 ng/mL as negative at 100 is reasonable but unstated.

reporting_issues.issue: The 10,000 ng/mL totals are cumulative over 1000 and 10,000 ng/mL (Table 1 note a), and carfentanil's entry in that column was measured at 4000 ng/mL; the Discussion speaks of 4000–10,000 ng/mL for carfentanil, though no 10,000 ng/mL carfentanil test is described.
reporting_issues.consequence: Cite the 21–24 of 28 as detection at 1000 ng/mL or above, and carfentanil as tested up to 4000 ng/mL.

reporting_issues.issue: Fig. 1C grades Rapid Response with fentanyl at 100 ng/mL as ++, Table 1 as +.
reporting_issues.consequence: Readings of borderline bands vary between runs or readers; with no replicates reported, single + or (+) cells are uncertain.

reporting_issues.issue: The abstract's counts (21–24 of 28) rest on the authors' reading of barely visible test bands as positive, contrary to the makers' rule the paper describes; by editors' recount under the makers' rule the cumulative counts are 19–21 of 28 and, at 100 ng/mL, 1–11 of 23.
reporting_issues.consequence: Claims should state the reading rule and concentration with any detection count.

reporting_issues.issue: The mixture experiment was done with one brand, and the main-text Fig. 2 shows two of the four brands; the mixture and co-presence results refer to supplementary figures. The statement that the additive effect is general is an expectation, not a result.
reporting_issues.consequence: Cite the mixture result for Nal van Minden only.

reporting_issues.issue: The Conclusion recommends testing injection solutions without further dilution, but the paper's own data show One Step false positives with ascorbic acid, which the authors included to model injection solutions, at 10 mg/mL and above.
reporting_issues.consequence: The recommendation is not reconciled with the ascorbic acid finding and should not be cited as tested.

design_detail: Laboratory evaluation of the first commercial nitazene immunoassay test strip, on reference standards dissolved in water and six powders from drug-market monitoring rather than on drug-checking samples or people. Filed as test-accuracy (METHODS §5.3, version 0.3.1): the units are prepared solutions, and QUADAS-2 is used for appraisal, as for sc_green_2020, because strip readings are compared with known content. One laboratory (Laboratory of Toxicology, Department of Bioanalysis, Ghent University, Belgium). Strips: BTNX Rapid Response nitazene test strips (competitive lateral flow immunoassay; maker's isotonitazene cut-off 2000 ng/mL), lot A DOAB23120001 and lot B DOAB24010002, obtained from Exchange Supplies (UK) about four months apart. Experiments: (1) limit of detection for isotonitazene at 500, 750, 1000, 1500, 2000 and 3000 ng/mL plus a blank, on three days in duplicate with both lots (6 replicates per concentration and lot); (2) cross-reactivity of 32 further nitazene analogues (33 with isotonitazene) with lot B, one strip at 3000 ng/mL and then at 1000 and/or 9000 ng/mL depending on the first result, plus brorphine at 1 mg/mL; (3) six powders from the Belgian Early Warning System on Drugs, each estimated above 90% one nitazene by LC-QTOF-MS, tested once at 1 mg/mL in tap water and once after tenfold dilution. Strips were photographed at 5 and 10 min in a fixed set-up and scored positive, negative or indeterminate by two blinded raters and by ImageJ; the 10-min readings are reported.
can_establish: The isotonitazene concentration at which two lots of the BTNX nitazene strip read positive in all replicates in water, which of 33 nitazene analogues gave positive single-strip readings at 1000, 3000 or 9000 ng/mL with one lot, which structural changes went with non-detection, and that six nearly pure nitazene powders read positive at about 1 and 0.1 mg/mL.
cannot_establish: Accuracy with real drug-checking samples, in which a nitazene may be a small part of a mixture with heroin, other opioids, stimulants or cutting agents (no nitazene-free, mixed or low-content samples were tested, and cross-reactivity with non-nitazene drugs was tested only for brorphine); detection limits for analogues other than isotonitazene; variation across more than two lots obtained four months apart; performance when people prepare and read strips at home; or any effect on behaviour or overdose.

sample.recruitment: Materials, not people: 33 nitazene reference standards and brorphine gifted by Cayman Chemical, prepared as 1 mg/mL stocks in methanol, acetonitrile, DMSO or methanol/DMSO and diluted in ultra-pure water (1.8% solvent); six powders obtained earlier in routine drug-market monitoring by the Belgian Early Warning System on Drugs (Sciensano) (Materials and methods › Materials, 1st paragraph).
sample.inclusion_exclusion: The analogue panel covers modifications at four positions of the 2-benzylbenzimidazole core and 14 of the 18 nitazenes notified in Europe between Q3 2019 and Q2 2024; flunitazene (a related halogenated analogue, clonitazene, was tested instead), N,N-dimethyl etonitazene, 6-methyl etodesnitazene and fluetonitazene (no standards yet) were not tested (Discussion, 5th paragraph; Fig. 4 legend). Powders: metonitazene, protonitazene, isotonitazene, butonitazene and two independently sourced N-pyrrolidino etonitazene samples.
sample.demographics: Not applicable (materials).
sample.attrition: None: no strip was invalid (Results, 1st paragraph). Compounds 9 and 16 were retested after a discrepant ImageJ result, and the retest replaced the first result in the categorization (Results › Cross-reactivity, 1st paragraph).
sample.selection_effects: All positives are pure standards or nearly pure powders (above 90% one nitazene), tested at concentrations around or far above the isotonitazene limit, and the only negatives are water and solvent blanks and nine non-reacting analogues: a two-gate design with no nitazene-free street samples, no mixtures and no low-content samples. The authors note that the powders are probably not representative of other real-world samples (Discussion, 7th paragraph).

exposure.measurement: Index test (Materials and methods › Methods › Nitazene test strip analysis, 1st to 3rd paragraphs): each strip taken from its sealed pouch, immersed for 15 s without exceeding the maximum line, laid on a non-absorbent flat surface and photographed with a smartphone at 5 and 10 min in a fixed set-up (Supplementary Information S1, not read). Reading rule: control and test lines = negative; control line only = positive; no line or a test line only = invalid; per the maker, any shade of test line = negative. Two raters blinded to sample identity scored each image + (confident positive), - (confident negative) or ? (at least one rater not confident); ImageJ scoring used a method tuned on a preliminary lot-A experiment with isotonitazene at 500–4000 ng/mL (Supplementary Information S2, not read).
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Not applicable (materials). Study concentrations, as free base: isotonitazene 500 to 3000 ng/mL; analogues at 3000, 1000 and/or 9000 ng/mL; brorphine 1 mg/mL; powders at 1 mg of powder in 1 mL of tap water (stirred briefly, some powder undissolved) and after tenfold dilution (Materials and methods › Methods › Limit of detection; Cross-reactivity; Testing of authentic powder samples).
exposure.polysubstance: Not applicable: each standard solution held one compound; the powders were estimated above 90% one nitazene from LC-QTOF-MS peak ratios, a semi-quantitative estimate, as the authors note. No mixture of a nitazene with other drugs or cutting agents was tested.

comparison.controls: Reference: known free-base concentrations of reference standards (working concentrations not verified analytically); LC-QTOF-MS identification of the main compound in each powder. Negative controls: water and 1.8% solvent blanks (methanol, acetonitrile, DMSO or methanol/DMSO), each tested at least once, and tap water for the powders.
comparison.matching: In the limit-of-detection study both lots were tested at the same concentrations on the same three days.
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Not applicable to materials. Not measured or not reported: detection limits for analogues other than isotonitazene; the 5-min readings (Supplementary Information S3, not read); salt forms and minor components of the powders; how much powder dissolved; cross-reactivity with non-nitazene drugs other than brorphine.

outcomes.instruments: Limit of detection for isotonitazene (lowest concentration at which all replicates read positive) for each lot; for each analogue, a single-strip score at 3000 ng/mL and at 1000 and/or 9000 ng/mL; positive or negative reading of the six powders at two concentrations; each by visual and by ImageJ scoring.
outcomes.validity_norms: The limit definition (all replicates positive) follows other strip evaluations. The cross-reactivity categories are single-strip results, not limits: isotonitazene read positive on a single lot-B strip at 1000 ng/mL although all-replicate positivity with that lot required 2000 ng/mL. ImageJ was tuned on lot-A isotonitazene strips like those it later scored.
outcomes.operationalization: Detected = a confident positive score at a tested concentration; indeterminate readings were not counted as positive. The authors' recommendation for practice, to read a faint test line as positive, differs both from the scoring used here and from the maker's instruction (Discussion, 8th paragraph).
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: Not applicable (descriptive; no statistical tests).
outcomes.assessor_blinding: The two visual raters were blinded to sample identity; ImageJ scoring was automated once tuned.

analysis.effect_sizes: No sensitivity or specificity is reported; for the powders the result amounts to 6 of 6 detected. Isotonitazene limit: 3000 ng/mL (lot A) and 2000 ng/mL (lot B), the same by visual and ImageJ scoring. Analogues: 24 of 33 positive at or below 9000 ng/mL (the editors' count from the compound lists agrees; 72.7%, with no interval because the panel is not a sample). Powders: 6 of 6 positive at both concentrations by both readings (Wilson 95% CI 61.0–100%, editors' calculation), in nearly pure single-nitazene powders only. Specificity cannot be estimated: the only negatives were blanks.
analysis.preregistration_detail: No protocol or registration is mentioned.
analysis.selective_reporting: The 10-min readings are reported because they had fewer indeterminate scores; the 5-min readings are only in Supplementary Information S3 (not read). The brorphine result and the powder purity calculations are marked data not shown; data are available on request. Two compounds were retested after a discrepant ImageJ pattern and the retest replaced the first result; no other compound was retested.
analysis.power: No sample-size reasoning. Six replicates per concentration for isotonitazene; one strip per concentration for each other analogue; six powders, giving a lower 95% bound of about 61% for sensitivity even with no misses (editors' calculation).

interpretation_gap.results_show: Two lots obtained four months apart detected isotonitazene in water in all replicates at 3000 and 2000 ng/mL. With one lot and single strips, 24 of 33 nitazene analogues read positive at 9000 ng/mL or less; the desnitazenes lacking the 5-nitro group (except 5-methyl etodesnitazene), 5-aminoisotonitazene and the two ethylene-linker analogues did not. Six nearly pure powders read positive at about 1 and 0.1 mg/mL. Specificity against other drugs and cutting agents, mixtures and low-content samples was not tested.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The abstract and conclusions are mostly limited to the conditions tested, but the abstract's six positive powders with “no observed false negatives” (Abstract › Results) were nearly pure, at nominal concentrations at least 30 times the isotonitazene limit (editors' calculation), and the Conclusion's statement that the strips show potential to recognize nitazenes in drug preparations in real-life settings goes beyond standards and pure powders tested without any negative or mixed samples. The Discussion's estimate that content down to 0.9–0.1% by weight may be detectable at 1–2 mg/mL (7th paragraph) uses 1000 ng/mL, below the measured isotonitazene limits; at those limits the editors' calculation gives 0.1–0.3%. The Discussion's statement that high concentrations of levamisole cause fentanyl-strip false positives (6th paragraph) cites, among others, a study (Halifax et al., 2024) that found none up to 100 mg/mL.

timeline.event: First detection of isotonitazene; 18 nitazene analogues notified to the EU early warning system between Q3 2019 and Q2 2024 (Introduction, 1st paragraph).
BTNX nitazene strips become commercially available in Q1 2024 (Introduction, 3rd paragraph).

Preliminary third-party data reported in the maker's white paper and cited in the Introduction: the CFSRE found 24 of 29 analogues cross-reacting at 3000 ng/mL, including metodesnitazene and etodesnitazene; the Chicago Recovery Alliance reported sensitivity of 100% and 89% at two sample dilutions and specificity of 100% in 12 street samples; not read.
Sisco et al. (2024): nitazene strip limits of 1000 ng/mL for metonitazene and 5000 ng/mL for N-piperidinyl etonitazene and for protonitazene, as cited in the Introduction; not read for this card.
This study published (28 August 2024).

replication.where_it_stands: The pattern that nitro-containing nitazenes are detected and most desnitazenes are not agrees with the maker's report and, for most compounds, with the CFSRE screen, but four compounds disagree with the CFSRE (metodesnitazene, etodesnitazene, butonitazene, 5-aminoisotonitazene), which the authors put down to sample preparation or lot. Single-strip results here and replicate-based limits from Sisco et al. (2024) are not directly comparable. No paper read for this batch tested nitazene strips on mixed or nitazene-free street samples.

funding.funder: Research Foundation–Flanders (FWO), grant 11I5623N to L.D.V. (Funding). Cayman Chemical gifted the reference standards (Acknowledgements).
funding.declared_conflicts: The authors declare that they have no conflict of interest (Ethics declarations).
funding.affiliations_note: All three authors from the Laboratory of Toxicology, Department of Bioanalysis, Ghent University. Several cited pharmacology studies are the authors' own, and one statement on the potency of ethylene-linker analogues rests on a submitted manuscript (Discussion, 5th paragraph). The powders came from the Belgian Early Warning System on Drugs and the strips were obtained from Exchange Supplies; no support from the strip maker is mentioned. A flag for closer reading, not a reason to discount.

what_would_settle_it: A blinded series of real drug-checking samples, including nitazene-free samples and mixtures in which a nitazene is a small fraction of heroin, other opioids, benzodiazepines or stimulants, tested on several lots against quantitative LC-MS, with replicate-based detection limits for the analogues on the market and a pre-specified rule for faint lines.

domains.note: Two-gate by design: pure standards and six nearly pure market-monitoring powders as positives, blanks as negatives; no nitazene-free street samples, mixtures or low-content samples. Applicability to drug checking is low.

The maker's instructions were followed with a fixed photographic set-up; two raters blinded to sample identity, with an indeterminate category, plus ImageJ. Minor concerns: the 10-min readings were chosen after seeing fewer indeterminate scores, ImageJ was tuned on lot-A strips and is detailed only in an unread supplement, and analogue results rest on single strips.
Reference standards at known free-base concentrations; LC-QTOF-MS identification of each powder's main compound (purity semi-quantitative). Working concentrations were not verified analytically.

Adaptive testing (the next concentration depended on the first result), one lot only for the analogues and powders, and retesting of two compounds only after a discrepant result, with the retest replacing the first; all strips were valid and all compounds are reported.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: QUADAS-2 is used because the study compares strip readings with known content (METHODS §5.3, diagnostic accuracy); the design is filed as test-accuracy (METHODS §5.3, version 0.3.1). The overall judgment follows the sample-selection domain: as an estimate of how the strips perform in drug checking, a set of pure positives and blank negatives is at high risk of overstating accuracy; as a laboratory measurement of the isotonitazene limit and of which analogues react, the study is well conducted (blinded raters, replicates, two lots, two scoring methods). Citable for: the isotonitazene limit of two lots (2000 and 3000 ng/mL); which analogues read positive at up to 9000 ng/mL with one lot, as single-strip results; non-detection at 9000 ng/mL of most desnitazenes, 5-aminoisotonitazene and the two ethylene-linker analogues; positive readings of six nearly pure powders. Not citable for: detection limits of other analogues, specificity, accuracy with mixed or low-content street samples, home use, or effects on behaviour or overdose.

preclinical.species_strain_sex: Not applicable: no organisms; the units are reference-standard solutions and market-monitoring powders dissolved in water.
preclinical.dose_route_schedule: Study conditions only: isotonitazene 500 to 3000 ng/mL (6 replicates per concentration and lot); other analogues at 1000, 3000 and/or 9000 ng/mL (one strip each); brorphine 1 mg/mL; powders at 1 mg/mL and 0.1 mg/mL in tap water; 15-s immersion; photographs at 5 and 10 min.
preclinical.resembles_human_use: Partly. The powder test was designed to resemble real-world use (about 1 mg/mL in tap water, brief stirring, undissolved powder left in place), following recommendations the authors cite, but the powders were nearly pure, the standards were in ultra-pure water with 1.8% organic solvent, readings were made from photographs by trained raters, and no mixed street sample was tested.

key_findings.finding: Two lots of BTNX Rapid Response nitazene strips (lot A DOAB23120001, lot B DOAB24010002; obtained about four months apart from Exchange Supplies, UK) were used per the product insert: immersed for 15 s below the maximum line, laid flat on a non-absorbent surface and photographed at 5 and 10 min. Reading rule (competitive assay): control and test lines = negative; control line only = positive; per the maker, any shade of test line = negative.
key_findings.locator: Materials and methods › Materials, 1st paragraph; Materials and methods › Methods › Nitazene test strip analysis, 1st paragraph; Discussion, 3rd paragraph

key_findings.finding: Two raters blinded to sample identity scored each image + (both confident of a positive), - (both confident of a negative) or ? (at least one not confident); no conflicts between a + and a - score occurred. ImageJ scoring was added, tuned on a preliminary lot-A experiment with isotonitazene at 500, 1000, 2000 and 4000 ng/mL and a blank.
key_findings.locator: Materials and methods › Methods › Nitazene test strip analysis, 2nd and 3rd paragraphs

key_findings.finding: No strip was invalid; all negative controls read negative by both methods; test lines were always fainter than control lines; fewer indeterminate scores occurred at 10 than at 5 min, so the 10-min readings are reported.
key_findings.locator: Results, 1st paragraph
key_findings.note: The 5-min readings are in Supplementary Information S3, not read.

key_findings.finding: Isotonitazene at 500, 750, 1000, 1500, 2000 and 3000 ng/mL (1.8% methanol in water) and a blank were tested on three days in duplicate with both lots (6 replicates per concentration and lot). With the limit defined as the lowest concentration at which all replicates read positive, it was 3000 ng/mL for lot A and 2000 ng/mL for lot B by both visual and ImageJ scoring. The maker's cut-off is 2000 ng/mL, with samples at 50% and 200% of the cut-off said to read all negative and all positive.
key_findings.locator: Materials and methods › Methods › Limit of detection, 1st paragraph; Results › Limit of detection, 1st paragraph; Fig. 2 (image)
key_findings.note: Replicate-level results from Fig. 2 (positives out of 6; figure read by AI reader 146 (second reader) on the full-size image and recorded in the saved text; not re-viewed by the adjudicator, as the browser was not available): lot A visual 0 at 500–1000, 1 at 1500, 2 at 2000 (others indeterminate), 6 at 3000; lot A ImageJ 0 up to 2000, 6 at 3000; lot B visual 0 at 500, 2 at 750, 2 at 1000, 3 at 1500, 6 at 2000 and 3000; lot B ImageJ 3 at 500, 2 at 750, 3 at 1000, 5 at 1500, 6 at 2000 and 3000; blanks 0. Lot B thus gave some positive readings at 25–50% of the cut-off, against the maker's statement that 50% of the cut-off reads all negative, so readings near the limit scatter.

key_findings.finding: Cross-reactivity (lot B): of 33 nitazene analogues including isotonitazene, 24 read positive at or below 9000 ng/mL (compounds 1–18, 25, 27–30 and 33) and 9 did not at 9000 ng/mL (compounds 19–24, 26, 31 and 32), by both visual and ImageJ scoring. Editors' count from the compound lists: 24 + 9 = 33.
key_findings.locator: Results › Cross-reactivity, 1st paragraph; Fig. 3 (image)

key_findings.finding: Visual scoring: 16 analogues positive at both 1000 and 3000 ng/mL, 7 at 3000 ng/mL only, and N-piperidinyl etonitazene (compound 16) at 9000 ng/mL only. ImageJ: 19 positive at 1000 and 3000 ng/mL and 5 at 3000 ng/mL only; compounds 2, 16 and 33 were positive by ImageJ but indeterminate by eye at 1000 ng/mL. Editors' check: both sets of lists add up to the 24 detected compounds.
key_findings.locator: Results › Cross-reactivity, 1st paragraph
key_findings.note: Fig. 3 differs from the text for compound 16 (N-piperidinyl etonitazene): its visual retest is positive at 3000 ng/mL (first visual test indeterminate) and positive at 9000 ng/mL in both tests. The text says the retest was used for the categorization, stating it for the ImageJ scoring; if the visual retest was used too, compound 16 is visually positive at 3000 ng/mL and none is positive only at 9000 ng/mL (a 16/8/0 split instead of 16/7/1). The text's visual split follows the first visual test (figure read by AI reader 146 (second reader) on the full-size image and recorded in the saved text; not re-viewed by the adjudicator, as the browser was not available).

key_findings.finding: Not detected at 9000 ng/mL: the six desnitazenes lacking the 5-nitro group (metodesnitazene, etodesnitazene, protodesnitazene, isotodesnitazene, N-pyrrolidino metodesnitazene, N-pyrrolidino etodesnitazene), 5-aminoisotonitazene, and the two analogues with an ethylene linker between the aromatic rings (ethylene nitazene, ethylene etonitazene). 5-Methyl etodesnitazene was the only desnitazene detected; changes at the para-benzyl position or the amine side chain did not prevent detection.
key_findings.locator: Results › Cross-reactivity, 2nd paragraph; Materials and methods › Materials, 1st paragraph (compound numbers); Fig. 4 (image)

key_findings.finding: Compounds 9 (N-pyrrolidino 4’-hydroxy nitazene) and 16 (N-piperidinyl etonitazene) were retested because ImageJ first scored them negative at 3000 and positive at 1000 ng/mL; on retesting ImageJ scored both positive at all three concentrations, and the retest was used. Isotonitazene and isotodesnitazene at 3000 ng/mL read positive and negative respectively at the minimum, middle and maximum immersion levels. Brorphine at 1 mg/mL showed no cross-reactivity (data not shown).
key_findings.locator: Results › Cross-reactivity, 1st paragraph; Fig. 3 legend

key_findings.finding: Six powders obtained earlier in routine drug-market monitoring by the Belgian Early Warning System on Drugs, which the paper calls sourced and never seized (metonitazene, protonitazene, isotonitazene, butonitazene, and N-pyrrolidino etonitazene twice), each with the nitazene as the major compound and an estimated purity above 90% from LC-QTOF-MS peak ratios: 1 mg of powder in 1 mL of tap water, stirred for 10 s and tested with one strip, then diluted tenfold and tested again; some powder remained undissolved in every mixture. All 12 readings were positive at 5 and 10 min by both methods; the tap-water blank was negative. Editors' calculation: 6 of 6 samples, Wilson 95% CI 61.0–100%.
key_findings.locator: Materials and methods › Materials, 1st paragraph; Materials and methods › Methods › Testing of authentic powder samples, 1st paragraph; Discussion, 7th paragraph; Results › Testing of authentic powder samples, 1st paragraph
key_findings.note: Nominally about 0.9 and 0.09 mg/mL of nitazene if fully dissolved, at least 30 times the isotonitazene limit (editors' calculation); no nitazene-free or mixed powder was tested. Two of the powders (isotonitazene and one N-pyrrolidino etonitazene) had been characterized earlier as pure and probably sold undiluted (Discussion, 7th paragraph).

key_findings.finding: The maker states that the strips are calibrated with isotonitazene (cut-off 2000 ng/mL), detect etonitazene, protonitazene and N-pyrrolidino etonitazene (cut-offs 1300–4500 ng/mL), do not detect metodesnitazene or etodesnitazene at 100 µg/mL, and do not cross-react with listed cutting agents (acetaminophen, caffeine, diphenhydramine), opioids (heroin, methadone, fentanyl) or other drugs (xylazine, MDMA, cocaine, ketamine) at 100 µg/mL or more; the authors did not repeat these specificity tests.
key_findings.locator: Introduction, 4th paragraph; Discussion, 6th paragraph

key_findings.finding: Earlier third-party data, as cited: the CFSRE found 24 of 29 analogues cross-reacting at 3000 ng/mL, including metodesnitazene and etodesnitazene; the Chicago Recovery Alliance reported sensitivity of 100% and 89% at two sample dilutions and specificity of 100% in 12 street samples; Sisco et al. reported limits of 1000 ng/mL (metonitazene) and 5000 ng/mL (N-piperidinyl etonitazene, protonitazene).
key_findings.locator: Introduction, 4th paragraph
key_findings.note: Second-hand: the CFSRE and Chicago Recovery Alliance data are cited from the maker's white paper; not read.

key_findings.finding: Differences from the CFSRE screen: metodesnitazene and etodesnitazene were not detected here at 9000 ng/mL (CFSRE: detected at 3000 ng/mL); butonitazene was detected here at 3000 ng/mL (CFSRE: not); 5-aminoisotonitazene was not detected here at 9000 ng/mL (CFSRE: detected at 3000 ng/mL). The authors suggest differences in sample preparation or strip lot.
key_findings.locator: Discussion, 4th paragraph

key_findings.finding: 14 of the 18 nitazenes notified in Europe from Q3 2019 to Q2 2024 were tested; the authors predict from structure that N,N-dimethyl etonitazene and fluetonitazene would react, make no prediction for 6-methyl etodesnitazene, and suggest that analogues with longer linkers, which generic laws may not cover, may escape detection.
key_findings.locator: Discussion, 5th paragraph

key_findings.finding: The Discussion estimates that, at the 1–2 mg/mL sample solutions recommended by others, nitazene content down to 0.9–0.1% by weight may be detectable, lower than the 11% N-pyrrolidino protonitazene reported in a powder sold as heroin in Ireland, and warns that traces below the cut-off may still cause dangerous opioid effects, that desnitazenes may be missed even in pure samples, and that incomplete dissolution may limit detection.
key_findings.locator: Discussion, 7th paragraph
key_findings.note: The 0.1% end uses 1000 ng/mL at 1 mg/mL, below the isotonitazene limits of both lots; at the measured limits (2000–3000 ng/mL) the editors' calculation gives 0.1–0.3% by weight at 1–2 mg/mL.

key_findings.finding: The authors conclude that the strips show potential to recognize most circulating nitazenes except desnitazenes, that a negative result does not mean a sample is safe, and that a positive result gives no information on identity, quantity or purity; they recommend reading a faint test line as positive as a precaution, unlike the maker's instruction.

reporting_issues.issue: The Discussion states that high concentrations (1 mg/mL or more) of MDMA, methamphetamine, levamisole and diphenhydramine cause fentanyl-strip false positives, citing Halifax et al. (2024), Norman et al. (2023) and Lockwood et al. (2021) (references 39, 45 and 57; Discussion, 6th paragraph); Halifax et al. found no levamisole cross-reactivity up to 100 mg/mL, and Lockwood et al. did not test levamisole (both read for this batch).
reporting_issues.consequence: Do not cite this paper for levamisole interference; of the three references only Norman et al. (2023), not read, could support it.

reporting_issues.issue: The cross-reactivity categories rest on one strip per compound per concentration with lot B, and isotonitazene read positive on a single strip at 1000 ng/mL although its all-replicate limit with lot B was 2000 ng/mL (Results › Cross-reactivity, 1st paragraph; Results › Limit of detection).
reporting_issues.consequence: The 1000, 3000 and 9000 ng/mL categories are not detection limits and should not be cited as such.

reporting_issues.issue: Two compounds were retested only because ImageJ gave a discrepant pattern, and the retest replaced the first result; for compound 16 the visual category (9000 ng/mL only) and the ImageJ category (1000 ng/mL) still differ ninefold, and Fig. 3 shows compound 16's visual retest positive at 3000 ng/mL, against the text's 'positive only at 9000 ng/mL' (Results › Cross-reactivity, 1st paragraph; Fig. 3 legend; Fig. 3).
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor; treat compound 16's reactivity as uncertain.

reporting_issues.issue: The 10-min readings are reported because they had fewer indeterminate scores; the 5-min readings appear only in a supplement (Results, 1st paragraph).
reporting_issues.consequence: Results at the earlier reading time may include more indeterminate scores; not checked here.

reporting_issues.issue: The Discussion's estimate of detectable content (0.9–0.1% by weight) rests at its lower end on 1000 ng/mL, below the isotonitazene limits measured with both lots (2000 and 3000 ng/mL) (Discussion, 7th paragraph).
reporting_issues.consequence: At the measured limits, about 0.1–0.3% by weight at 1–2 mg/mL (editors' calculation).

reporting_issues.issue: The Methods attribute the 1–2 mg/mL sample-preparation recommendation to the CFSRE with reference 40, which is the maker's product insert; the Discussion cites the same recommendation to references 40 and 50 (the insert and a New Zealand Drug Foundation page) (Materials and methods › Methods › Testing of authentic powder samples; Discussion, 7th paragraph).
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor citation mismatch; the source of the recommendation is the maker's insert and the New Zealand page.

reporting_issues.issue: The brorphine result and the powder purity calculations are marked data not shown, and the data are available only on request (Results › Cross-reactivity; Materials and methods › Methods › Testing of authentic powder samples; Data availability).
reporting_issues.consequence: These cannot be checked.
